newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Supermarket to Asia body aims to cut barriers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Supermarket to Asia body aims to cut barriers.

text.p: Australia's Supermarket to Asia Council would assemble government and industry leaders to work together to remove barriers to greater exports of food products to the Asian region, Australian Prime Minister John Howard said.

Howard told the annual meeting of the Australian Food Council Australian food producers were among the most efficient in the world and Australia had a natural advantage of producing products in a relatively clean environment.

To tap the "significant opportunity" of Asia's total food market, estimated at A$685 billion by 2000, including imports of more than A$83 billion, producing quality food on farms and properties was not enough, Howard said.
"We then have to get it to markets at a good price, we have to add value to our raw products and we have to promote what we produce," he said.

"Australia produces the food the region needs. Instead of knocking on doors to markets, it's time we took the hinges off the doors so that neighbouring consumers benefit, our food producers benefit and Australia as a whole benefits," he said.
The Supermarket to Asia Council, chaired by Howard, will include four other senior ministers and senior representatives of business, including retail, food and transport.
Representatives would work hand-in-hand with government to remove unnecessary regulation, reduce the cost of doing business and increase opportunities for new markets, Howard said.
The government had committed A$6 million over three years to boost efforts to clear quarantine barriers to exports, he said.
Australia recently signed an agreement with the Philippines that would allow access of Australian fruit previously banned, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
